intro.title: Binary Search
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that implements the binary search algorithm to efficiently find a target value in a sorted array. You will learn the core concept of divide-and-conquer, where the search space is repeatedly halved by comparing the target to the middle element. The main constructs involved are arrays, while loops, and conditional logic to manage indices and comparisons. By the end, you will understand how binary search achieves O(log n) time complexity, making it much faster than linear search for large datasets.
intro.usecase: Binary search is essential for efficiently finding items in sorted datasets, a common requirement in modern applications. You'll use it when implementing autocomplete suggestions in search bars, filtering large product catalogs in e-commerce sites, or navigating sorted user lists in admin dashboards. As a developer, you might apply binary search to optimize performance when handling sorted arrays of timestamps in analytics tools or implementing pagination with sorted results. This algorithm ensures your applications remain responsive even when processing thousands of items.
